source: Let's build a game where the player throws balls at a target to score points. The goal is to hit as many targets as possible before a 30-second timer runs out. The ball spawns at the bottom middle of the screen. Players long press on the ball to grab it, swipe and let go to throw it. The ball is thrown in the direction they swipe. The faster they swipe, the harder the ball is thrown. Targets can appear in one of three rows along the foreground, middle ground, or background, and may appear anywhere to the left or right of center. When the player hits a target, it is removed and replaced with another in a different position along the same row. Targets in the background are worth 25 points. Targets in the middle ground are worth 10, and in the foreground 5. Visually, the game is themed after a carnival booth with wooden targets and bright red balls.

image_prompt.text: Wooden carnival targets standing in three rows at different depths, each row registering a different point value
Depth cues along the booth separating the foreground, middle and background rows so the player can read how far each target is
A fixed ball position at the bottom middle of the booth where each new ball appears

layout_placement.text: Hit detection on each target: 25 points in the back row, 10 in the middle, 5 in the front
The ball spawn position, centred at the near edge of the play space
When a target is hit it is removed and a replacement appears at a different position in the same row
A 30 second round timer; the score is how many targets were hit before it runs out

notes: Party & Casual was considered - this reads as a carnival minigame - but Sports Target Sport covers a directed range with discrete targets exactly, so only Sports was used.
The layout is described relative to the camera (bottom middle of the screen, three depth rows) rather than in world terms.

open_questions.ask: How far back is the third row meant to feel - a few metres like a real booth, or exaggerated?
Is the booth enclosed with a back wall and side walls, or open?

theme: Carnival booth - painted wood targets, bright red balls, fairground colours

coverage_missing.ask: How deep should the three rows be spaced?
How many targets are up at once in each row?

answers.ask: How far back is the third row meant to feel - a few metres like a real booth, or exaggerated?
answers.answer: Use a few metres like a real carnival booth; keep the three rows compact and clearly readable.

answers.ask: Is the booth enclosed with a back wall and side walls, or open?
answers.answer: Make it enclosed with a back wall and side walls, like a standard carnival throwing booth.
